title: Why our soaps take a month
dek: How cold-process soap is made, and why we wait 21 to 28 days before packing it.

body.p: Our natural soaps are made the slow way, in small batches at our partner's unit near Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh.
In cold-process soap making, oils such as coconut and castor are mixed with lye at low temperatures, poured into moulds and cut into bars. Freshly cut bars still hold a lot of water.
So we leave the bars to cure for 21 to 28 days before they are checked and packed. As the bars cure, excess water gradually evaporates, helping them become firmer and last longer in use.

body.h: How to make a bar last
body.p: Keep it on a soap dish that drains, out of the stream of water. A dry bar lasts much longer than one sitting in a puddle.
Our current soaps include Kuppaimeni (Indian nettle), Hibiscus & Rose and Tomato Extract. Each product page explains its key ingredients and how to use it.

title: Moringa oil for your face: how much, when, and for whom
dek: Two or three drops at night is usually enough. Here is why, and who should skip it.

body.p: Moringa is the drumstick tree, sahjan, that grows across much of India. Its seeds give a light oil. For our oil, the seeds are dried in the sun before they are pressed, and nothing else is added.

Like most plant oils, moringa seed oil is an emollient: it softens the surface of the skin and helps it feel less dry. There is no good evidence that it changes wrinkles or elasticity, so we do not suggest it does.
Two or three drops is enough for face and neck. Warm them between your palms and press them on after your mist or gel at night. Night is when an oil has the most time to work.
If your skin is oily or breaks out easily, try a single drop on a few nights first, or stay with the aloe gel. As with anything new, patch test on your inner arm.

title: A winter evening ritual for dry skin and heels
dek: When the air turns dry, add two small steps to your evening.

body.p: In north Indian winters, skin that was fine in October can feel tight by December. Heels crack, lips peel. A good evening ritual helps, and it does not need many products.
Cleanse with a mild bar, mist with rose water, then press two or three drops of moringa oil onto your face. If you prefer a gel, use the aloe gel with vitamin E.
Finish with a rich lip balm, and massage the ghee foot butter into your heels before putting on cotton socks. Our founder tells us older customers often reorder it for dry, cracked heels.
Cracks that are deep, bleed or hurt need medical care, not just a foot butter.
